blocking_questions.question: What numerical value or iteration-dependent schedule for Equation 16's median-attraction coefficient a4 was used in the MMA runs reported in Tables 5-7 and 9-10?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: Equation 16 defines a4 as a positive social-attraction coefficient, but Table 4 reports a1, a2, beta, d, and fl without an a4 value. Mayfly's MedianWeight=0.5 is a compatibility choice, not a paper-derived value.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: The exact finite a4 value or complete executable schedule, including whether it differs between benchmark functions, governor conditions, or iterations.
acceptable_primary_evidence: The Tables 5-10 MMA source code and experiment configuration
A dated author clarification giving the exact value or schedule

blocking_questions.question: Does Equation 15 rank and take the middle position from males only, females only, or the combined male and female population, and at what lifecycle point is that pool sampled?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The prose says all mayfly individuals, Equation 15 uses male-position notation x, and Equation 16 applies the result only to male velocity. The article does not state whether n denotes one sex or both, or whether ranking occurs before or after movement, mating, and survivor selection.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: An executable definition of the candidate pool, objective-value ranking direction and tie handling, odd/even rule, and lifecycle point for every median calculation.
blocking_questions.units: candidate identities, ranks, and lifecycle stages
acceptable_primary_evidence: A dated author clarification defining the complete median lifecycle

blocking_questions.question: What offspring count, crossover-coefficient distribution and draw granularity, mutation scale, and complete mating/mutation settings were used for MMA in Tables 5-10?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article gives the generic mating and Gaussian-mutation equations and says round(0.05 times the male count) individuals mutate, but Table 4 does not provide the offspring count, crossover-coefficient range/distribution, Gaussian sigma, or whether draws are per pair, offspring, or coordinate.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: Exact offspring and survivor counts, crossover distribution/range with draw granularity, mutation selection rule and sigma, simultaneous-versus-sequential offspring semantics, and any benchmark/governor differences.
blocking_questions.units: offspring, probabilities or fractions, dimensionless crossover coefficients, and decision-space mutation scale
acceptable_primary_evidence: The Tables 5-10 source and configuration implementing mating and mutation
A dated author clarification defining every operator parameter and random draw

blocking_questions.question: How were positions and velocities initialized, and what velocity limits and position/velocity boundary-repair rules were used in the benchmark and governor experiments?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article says two sex-specific populations are randomly placed and positions and velocities are initialized, but it does not state the distributions, initial velocity bounds, clipping/reflection/resampling rules, or whether algorithms shared initial populations.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: The exact position and velocity distributions and bounds, random-draw granularity, repair rules after every update/operator, and across-algorithm/run sharing policy.
blocking_questions.units: decision-space and velocity units, distributions, and draws per candidate or coordinate
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original initialization and boundary-handling source
A dated author clarification giving deterministic executable rules

blocking_questions.question: Which objective calls count toward each function-evaluation limit, and how does a run stop when the remaining budget cannot cover a full update, offspring, or mutation batch?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The paper specifies function-dependent FE ceilings but does not define whether initialization, parent re-evaluation, male/female movement, offspring, mutants, rejected candidates, or repaired candidates count, nor partial-generation stopping and final-best selection.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: A per-stage objective-call ledger, iteration indexing, partial-generation rule, target/early stopping behavior, and final-result selection convention.
acceptable_primary_evidence: The benchmark driver with objective-call counters
A dated author clarification defining the complete budget and stopping convention

blocking_questions.question: Can the original MMA implementation, batch drivers, random-number generator and ordered seeds/states, and raw per-run benchmark and governor outputs be supplied?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The paper reports 30 benchmark runs and 35 governor runs but no generator, seeds, saved states, code, or ordered trial data. Only aggregate tables and figure-only convergence/response outputs are public.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: Versioned source/configuration files with checksums; generator/version and ordered seed or state mapping; and ordered terminal values, iteration counts, convergence histories, PID gains, and response metrics for every algorithm, function, condition, and run.
blocking_questions.units: source files, checksums, generator states, objective values, iterations, PID gains, and response metrics
acceptable_primary_evidence: A publisher or institutional archive deposited by the authors

blocking_questions.question: Can the exact MATLAB/Simulink hydro-turbine governor model and simulation configuration used for Tables 9-10 and Figures 8-9 be supplied?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: The article prints the transfer functions, two Table 8 parameter tuples, a block-diagram figure, 20-second horizon, PID bounds, and disturbance size, but not the Simulink file, MATLAB release, solver, step size/tolerances, block settings, PID form, saturation, initial conditions, disturbance timing, or numerical ITAE integration rule.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: The versioned model and MATLAB scripts plus release/toolbox versions, solver and sample-time settings, every block parameter and initial condition, PID convention and limits, disturbance injection, and executable ITAE calculation.
blocking_questions.units: model files, software versions, seconds, solver tolerances, PID gains, and ITAE integration units
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original SLX/MDL model and governor experiment scripts
A dated author clarification plus an equivalent versioned executable model

blocking_questions.question: What are the intended corrections and underlying raw values for the printed F10 domain, F18 MMA best/median ordering, and Table 9 success-rate omission?
blocking_questions.known_evidence: Table 3 prints F10 as [65.536,65.536] without a negative lower bound; Table 7 prints the minimizing F18 median below the reported best; and the Table 9 prose says success rate is listed although the table contains no success-rate row.
blocking_questions.required_answer_shape: An author correction or original source/configuration and ordered trials establishing the intended F10 bounds, correct F18 statistics, and both working-condition success-rate definition, numerator, denominator, and values.
blocking_questions.units: decision-space bounds, objective values, successes, trials, and percent
acceptable_primary_evidence: The original benchmark/governor source and raw trials
A publisher correction or dated author clarification backed by the source data

exact_preset_gate.rule: An mpma-2022 exact algorithm preset and benchmark runner may be added only after all five questions have non-null answers backed by cited primary evidence and the resulting configuration, operators, lifecycle, and evaluation ledger pass equation-, accounting-, and source-conformance tests.

reproduction_comparison_gate.rule: A full Tables 5-10 reproduction comparison additionally requires all three comparison questions to be resolved. A benchmark-only comparison must identify the unavailable governor model explicitly; aggregate-only comparisons must remain descriptive and must not imply historical-run identity or pairing.

correspondence_draft.subject: Request for MMA/MPMA Tables 5-10 implementation, protocol, and trial data
correspondence_draft.body:
Dear Professor Xu and co-authors,

I am implementing the protocol from your 2022 IEEE Access article, An Improved Mayfly Optimization Algorithm Based on Median Position and Its Application in the Optimization of PID Parameters of Hydro-Turbine Governor (doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2022.3160714), and would like to reproduce Tables 5-10 faithfully. Could you please share the original MMA implementation, benchmark and governor drivers/configurations, raw trials, and MATLAB/Simulink governor model? For an executable preset, could you also clarify: (1) Equation 16's a4 value or schedule; (2) whether Equation 15's ranked median covers males, females, or both and when it is calculated; (3) offspring count, crossover-coefficient distribution/draw granularity, mutation sigma, and survivor settings; (4) position/velocity initialization, limits, repair, and shared-initialization policy; and (5) exact function-evaluation accounting and partial-generation stopping? For validation, please also provide the generator and ordered seeds/states for the 30 benchmark and 35 governor runs; model, solver, sample-time, PID, disturbance, and ITAE-integration settings; and the intended corrections/raw values for the F10 range, F18 best/median ordering, and omitted Table 9 success rates. Version identifiers or checksums and ordered per-run objective, convergence, PID, iteration, ITAE, overshoot, and adjustment-time data would make the comparison auditable.

Thank you for your time.
